name: Ambrose 'Uncle' Pell
languages: Norwegian (from his mother, rusty but good for the fishing families)
equipment: A three-piece grey suit, shiny at the knees, a gold watch chain with no watch on it, and a bowler hat
.32 pocket pistol (Savage 1907), 8 rounds loaded, in the inside pocket where it ruins the suit
Straight razor, pearl-handled, for shaving and for emphasis
The shoeshine stand on the Hall of Justice steps: a high chair, a box of brushes, polish and rags, and a sign: PELL'S SHINE, 15 CENTS, ADVICE FREE
A card file of contacts in a cigar box: four hundred names, with notes in a code of his own
A pass key to the Hotel Meridian, from his days as its house detective; Walsh has never had the locks changed
A notebook of who owes him what, which he never needs to look at
A flask of rye, a tin of peppermints and a roll of nickels
features: Plain Dealing (Small-Town origin: once per long rest, roll an Insight check against a lie with advantage and, on a success, learn whether they lie to protect themselves or someone else; working people start one step friendlier toward him)

Favors Owed (Fixer: a pool of five favors from the city's powerful and not-so-powerful, refilled at the start of each new case; one favor buys a name, a file for an hour, a man released from a precinct house, a meeting or a warning; two buy something big, like a story kept out of the paper; every favor spent is one he owes)
Know Everybody (Fixer: proficiency bonus doubled for Persuasion and Streetwise checks)

Read the Room (Fixer, 2nd level: after a minute of conversation, an Insight check against a person's Deception tells him one of their goals, one of their fears, or whether one thing they said was a lie, and who in the room they are most afraid of)
Circle: City Hall (Fixer, 3rd level: once per case, a city-level favor, such as a permit, an inspection, a zoning ruling or a file from the Hall of Records after hours, costs one favor less)

Fast Talk (Fixer, 5th level: as an action, a creature that can hear and understand him makes a WIS save, DC 14, or hesitates, losing its next reaction and having disadvantage on its next attack roll; his favor pool increases by one)

Pass Key (Hotel Dick background: he knows the inside of every hotel in Port Calloway, the house detectives, the night clerks and the bellboys, and his old Meridian pass key still opens every door above the mezzanine)

personality.traits: I sit on my shoeshine chair on the Hall of Justice steps and the whole city walks past me, and most of it stops. I call everybody 'nephew' or 'niece'. I never write anything down where it can be read. I never say no; I say 'that'll take some doing'.
personality.ideals: Everybody in this city needs something from somebody else. A man who knows who needs what is never out of work and never alone.
personality.bonds: The steps, and the people on them: lawyers, clerks, cops, bail bondsmen, defendants' mothers. And Walt Embry, whom I have known since he was a rookie with his hat on wrong.
personality.flaws: I owe favors too, and some of them are to men on Larch Hill. When one of them calls a favor in, I will have to decide what I am, and I have spent twenty years arranging never to have to decide.

appearance: A plump, pink, bald man of sixty-one with white mutton-chop whiskers, small shrewd blue eyes, a gold tooth and a voice like warm molasses. He wears an old three-piece suit and a bowler hat in all weathers, and shines shoes with a speed and delicacy that look like a magic trick. He smells of shoe polish, peppermint and bay rum.
backstory: Ambrose Pell came to Port Calloway from a wheat town in the dry country east of the mountains in 1910, at nineteen, with a cardboard suitcase and a talent for being liked. He was a bellboy at the Hotel Meridian, then its night clerk, then for twenty years its house detective, which is to say the man who knew which senator was in which room with whom, and who kept quiet about it, and was owed for it. When a new owner retired him in 1946 he bought a shoeshine stand on the Hall of Justice steps for $40, and he has made more money from it since, in favors and in information, than he ever did at the Meridian. Everybody who goes into the Hall of Justice has their shoes shined by Pell, or walks past him, which is the same thing. He is the agency's fixer, informant and occasional banker, and he has never once asked Walt to repay a loan. He knows Dunleavy, Maddox, Lusk, Sloane and Vantreight, and he owes something to all of them.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Pell is the party's switchboard: when they are stuck, they go to the steps, have their shoes shined, and leave with a name, an address, or a warning. Use him to deliver leads the party missed (the watchman's island, the Meridian register, Dahl's reputation, Dunleavy's request for the DA detail), always at a price: a favor, a dollar, or a story he can trade. He is a companion who does not go on operations; he is too old and too well known. His pass key to the Meridian is how the party gets into room 914 in pa-scenario-003.
dmNotes.voice: Slow, warm, folksy, with a dry-country drawl and a habit of answering questions with stories about 1923. Calls men 'nephew' and women 'niece'. When he is serious, the folksiness drops away all at once, and he speaks in short clear sentences, and that is how you know it is serious.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: stay useful, which is to say stay alive and on the steps. Secondary: look after Walt and his people, whom he regards as his family. Tertiary: never be made to choose between them and the men he owes.
dmNotes.secrets: In 1946, as the Meridian's house detective, he was asked by Lt. Dunleavy to forget that Earl Haskin, Vantreight's plant manager, had a room at the Meridian on the night of the Halvorsen fire and received a visitor at two in the morning: a man with burns on his hands who checked out before dawn. Pell forgot. He has the night register page in his cigar box. It is the only evidence anywhere of the torch, and Pell will produce it only if Vantreight calls in a favor first, or if Walt asks him directly and tells him why. Second secret: Vantreight once paid off a debt of Pell's, and Pell owes him one favor, unnamed. In pa-scenario-003 or 004, Vantreight calls it in: he wants to know where the original statement is.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: avuncular, fond, and always a little bit calculating. Toward Walt: like a father toward a son who did not turn out as planned and turned out better. Toward Becerra: approving. Toward Dunleavy: flattery and fear. Toward Vantreight: fear, mostly. Toward Nora Kessling: he knew her father, and he gives her free shines.
